increment.observedProblem: The current immutable public release honestly exposes a host-adaptive Skill and bounded continuity, repair and resource fixtures, but it mostly declares rather than closes the larger finite-autonomy promise. The current long Codex task crossed automatic compaction without YIYUAN Accord surfacing a carrier-fitness decision, and the existing model contains a capability meta-model without a complete collaboration-control coverage map. A single handoff Hook or more host adapters would address symptoms while leaving users to operate many other avoidable discovery, configuration, routing, topology, verification, update and cleanup mechanics.
increment.hypothesis: A lightweight relation-and-constraint model can preserve an open demand-capability universe while making finite collaboration-control obligations explicit. Identifying unclosed obligations, degraded or uncertain relations, coordination and verification risks, then proving one full collaboration-closure slice with native no-op, maintained or composed help, bounded authorship, correction, resource and lifecycle paths can increase real autonomy without reviving a universal runtime, copying the pre-Accord implementation or making a current host list the product ceiling.

facts: Codex and Claude expose Skills for relevant implicit use, but availability and installation are not task-time behavior proof.

Current Codex plugin Hooks support SessionStart for startup, resume, clear and compact; compact-matched context reaches the immediate post-compaction continuation. Command and MCP handlers are supported, prompt and Agent handlers are skipped, and each new or changed non-managed Hook hash requires user review and trust.

Current Claude plugin Hooks support SessionStart for startup, resume, clear, compact and fork; plain standard output becomes context. The same Hook lifecycle runs in local CLI, IDE and Desktop sessions, while Cloud uses its own repository or account-carried conditions.

Claude can reload installed or development plugin Skills, Agents, Hooks, MCP and LSP surfaces in-session. Current Codex documentation supports marketplace refresh and plugin reinstall or restart paths but does not establish equivalent active-session plugin hot reload.
inferences: A compact SessionStart reminder is a candidate activation and post-compaction context path that need not inspect transcripts, add state, run per prompt or create a second control plane; actual host firing and effect remain separate evidence.

A UserPromptSubmit Hook would add unavoidable per-turn overhead and Codex cannot narrow it with a matcher; Stop prompt or Agent Hooks add model cost and lack current Codex portability; a Runtime or MCP is not yet justified for static activation.
Host lifecycle differences require capability-conditioned update and rollback, not a false cross-host hot-reload claim.
unknowns: Fresh task-time behavior and measurable net help remain unverified.
Codex active-session plugin hot reload is not established by current official documentation.
Claude client behavior through the user's current third-party model route and Cloud behavior remain separate condition-fit evidence lanes.

complexityBudget.rule: Complexity checkpoints are revisable release guardrails, not product invariants, capability deletion targets or reasons to reject a demonstrated collaboration-closure need. The active bounded-autonomy increment raises the planning checkpoint to at most 78 tracked files and 260000 product-code-and-test bytes with at least five percent headroom so one release note, bounded host mechanism, tests and evidence can be admitted without pretending that the previous public release's three spare slots are a permanent architecture. None is a growth target. Count code, prompts, context, state, processes, evidence, user cognition, latency, interference, recovery, maintenance and retirement. At each breach or same-purpose repair, compare deletion, native delegation, composition, replacement and bounded addition; retain only outcome-bearing semantics or mechanisms with verified lifecycle and cleanup.

processLossControl.alignmentRule: Keep latest demand and corrections aligned through goal, authority, route, implementation, evidence, acceptance and claim. At material correction, effect or phase boundaries, locate the earliest divergence, replay affected downstream work and preserve unrelated accepted truth.
processLossControl.resourceRule: Observe current demand and capacity, attribute identity, owner, lease and state, admit minimum sufficient concurrency and budget, rebalance or degrade under pressure, release only attributable task-owned exposure through authorized native controls, and independently verify post-state and residue. Shared or unknown ownership is never reclaimed automatically; sufficient native whole-loop governance is a no-op and an Accord-specific mechanism retirement trigger.
processLossControl.carrierRule: Use current source-bound host signals when reliable; if capacity is unavailable, record unknown and transition conservatively. No universal turn count, context size, token percentage or summary ratio is product authority.
processLossControl.correctionRule: A material correction, failure, later rule or revision supersedes affected current-candidate evidence from the earliest dependency boundary and requires that boundary and every downstream gate to be replayed while unrelated accepted truth remains stable. A repeated correction or failed same-purpose mechanism pauses the current shape until premise, interface and representation are reconsidered; deletion, replacement, recomposition, native-host delegation and bounded addition are all considered. There is no universal add-or-subtract default, while L2 requires a deletion or replacement attempt before another same-purpose repair layer. Authority surfaces form a reviewable versioned current set; their merge, split, replacement or retirement requires explicit provenance-preserving schema and verifier migration plus the same earliest-boundary replay.
processLossControl.continuingCalibration: Post-release failures may update Golden Tasks, narrow a claim, simplify or retire a projection, or open one new bounded increment; release status does not freeze learning.
processLossControl.boundedAutonomyRule: At each material phase, recompute the latest outcome obligations, relevant live relations and constraints, healthy effective capabilities, genuinely non-delegable human judgment, unclosed obligations and coordination or verification risks. Preserve the latest correction through closure path, implementation, evidence, acceptance and claim.
